instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Mental health tech company offering an app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program with human therapist chat support. 18,000 active users. Clinical evidence from a published RCT showing 40% reduction in PHQ-9 scores. Expanding into corporate wellness programs and evaluating AI-supported therapist productivity tools. Multi-department organization with formalized budgets, quarterly business reviews, and a dedicated strategy function. We have invested in core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) but these are not always well-integrated. Innovation is a standing agenda item at board level with annual investment allocated, but execution velocity varies across business units.
answers.pastInitiatives: Innovation is not a formalized function in our organization. We occasionally try new tools or workflows when a team member champions them, but these are isolated, grassroots efforts without executive sponsorship, budget allocation, or structured measurement of outcomes.
answers.strategicGoals: The board has mandated that 25% of revenue should come from products or services that did not exist 3 years ago. This requires us to systematically explore adjacent markets, new customer segments, and alternative monetization models. We are open to both organic build initiatives and strategic acquisitions of small, innovative companies that can serve as diversification platforms.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads: one focused on core product innovation and one on exploratory/new business model prototyping. We also have 2 dedicated data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.

input.changes_since_last: Product launch successful — 4 new features shipped. Customer NPS improved 20 points. Backlog of technical debt growing.

opportunities.title: Establish a Formal M&A/Adjacent Market Scouting Unit
opportunities.rationale: The board has mandated 25% revenue from new sources, requiring systematic exploration beyond current product lines. Moving from ad-hoc interest to a structured scouting function is critical for meeting this mandate and realizing diversification goals.

first_actions: Draft charter defining M&A criteria (e.g., technology fit, regulatory safety).
Allocate dedicated internal time/budget within the exploratory squad for scouting reports.
Identify 3 potential small target companies or adjacent market verticals to build initial due diligence case studies.
resources_needed: Executive sponsorship from the CEO/Board Chair
execution_plan.success_metric: Completion of 3 detailed 'Build vs. Buy' feasibility reports within six months.
milestones: First two target company analyses completed.
Presentation to the Executive Committee recommending a path forward (build/buy).

opportunities.title: Formalize and Industrialize the Innovation Function (Stage-Gate)
opportunities.rationale: Current innovation efforts are siloed, grassroots, and lack executive governance. To scale successfully, the process must move from 'occasional' to a structured, funded function that measures outcomes systematically and manages resource contention.

first_actions: Develop a mandatory Stage-Gate framework for all new initiatives (Idea -> Concept -> Pilot -> Scale).
Mandate formal project charter creation at the outset of every initiative, defining success metrics and required resources.
Implement a quarterly portfolio review mechanism managed by the Strategy function to kill or accelerate stalled projects.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in 'stalled' or undefined initiatives by 50% within one year.
milestones: First three major projects successfully run through the new gate process.
Formal resource allocation model linked to project stage.

next_steps.action: Define and execute a technical debt reduction roadmap, dedicating 20% of engineering capacity in Q3/Q4 to stabilizing core systems.
Hold a dedicated cross-functional workshop (R&D, Strategy, Ops) to finalize the Stage-Gate process and assign owners for governance checks.
Formalize Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for the exploratory squad, linking them directly to the board's diversification mandate.
next_steps.owner: Head of Business Development / Board Liaison

key_weaknesses: Poor integration between core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) leading to operational drag and data silos.
Lack of standardized governance mechanism for innovation, resulting in resource diffusion across multiple uncoordinated efforts.
Technical debt accumulating rapidly despite successful product feature launches.

improvements: Strong evidence of clinical efficacy (RCT published) and positive market validation. The 20-point NPS increase is a significant operational success.
Leadership alignment on strategic diversification goals, driven by board mandate.
persistent_gaps: The formal process remains underdeveloped; execution velocity is hindered by structural/cultural friction rather than technical capability.
Technical debt accumulation poses an increasing risk to product stability and future feature scaling.
achieved_milestones: Successful launch of four new features, demonstrating core development capacity.
Identification of the need for structured diversification funding/approach from the Board level.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Significant operational improvement (NPS, features) and a clear strategic mandate from the board for diversification. The focus shifts now from 'if' to 'how' systematic innovation will be executed.
